items.q: So I took the job. And I stayed with Sarah for the better part of two years.

ctx.x: friend of mine since back during the Chicago days... Which, if I didn't mention it, when I was in Chicago with Trummy Young, one of the groups there was Stuff Smith, who had a trio with Jimmy Jones and John Levy playing bass -- Jimmy Jones playing piano and Stuff Smith, violin. So I had known Jimmy for quite a while, and we were good friends, and we had just a real piano comrade thing going. So this was a dreadful thing to hear. But in hearing it, there was nothing that... You know, you can't do anything about…

So I took the job. And I stayed with Sarah for the better part of two years. Jimmy Jones endured this operation and everything, and he came out of the hospital, and he was well, and he came back to his job. If I can get ahead a little bit, to just complete this story, this is in 1954. I think five or six years later, during 1960, George Treadwell died of cancer, and Jimmy Jones lived a good 20 or 25 years after that. So I would say to anybody, don't ever predict anybody's death, because no one knows when that's…

But to go back to the Sarah Vaughan days, naturally, we were happy with each other, because we had worked together in the Eckstine band, and we'd always been good friends, and actually hang-out buddies when we were in the band. When I joined the trio, it was somewhat the same way. I played my

ctx.x: Because Joe has been drinking a little too much. I don't think I want to ride with him." So we said, "Sure!"

In the meanwhile, the theatre that we'd just played in Washington before had a show, and they had a line of chorus girls, who after that engagement were not going to be working for a while. And one of these girls was a friend of Sarah. Sarah asked her to come along with her as an assistant, to help her dress and whatever. Her name was Daisy. I don't remember Daisy's last name. But Daisy was also with Joe. She and Sarah had ridden out there with him.

So when Sarah asked if she could ride back with me -- fine. She gets in the car with us. And we had an expression that we used to use. All bands and groups have things that they say. And when something looks funny or something looks different, we used to just say "There he go" or "There he goes" or something like that. So we were riding down the highway, and we were doing the speed limit, and there's a slight drizzle, rain. All of a sudden, after we had gone about a mile or two, this car whizzed past us, and who…
